question.text: Kamat Family Office Ltd., a body corporate, subscribes as LP in Himalaya Growth Fund. Under PMLA Rules, the AIF must identify Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) of Kamat Family Office. The controlling ownership threshold for identifying a UBO of a COMPANY/TRUST is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules, UBO identification: (a) for a COMPANY or TRUST, the threshold is 25% of ownership/entitlement; (b) for a PARTNERSHIP FIRM or UNINCORPORATED ASSOCIATION OF INDIVIDUALS, the threshold is 15% of ownership/entitlement. Records must be maintained for minimum 5 years from cessation of transactions. The Trap: Option A (10%) is FDI threshold, not PMLA UBO. Option B (15%) is for partnerships/unincorporated associations — swap trap. Option D (51%) is majority control, not UBO. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XXIV AML test UBO thresholds. FATCA/CRS use similar but distinct thresholds. SEBI FPI Regulations test UBO separately. Banking KYC (RBI) also uses 25%/15% split — consistent cross-industry. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'UBO look-through' for every institutional LP: pull shareholding down to ultimate natural persons. For trust LPs, trace through settlor/protector/beneficiary. If no natural person meets 25%, document 'senior managing official' as deemed UBO per PMLA Rules. SEBI inspectors routinely sample UBO files during AIF audits.
